chunks: And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, that he said:
Regarding a man who intentionally kills his slave, he said: “I prefer that he frees a slave, fasts two consecutive months, and feeds sixty needy people; then repentance should be after that.”

key_terms.سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا: sixty needy persons to be fed
key_terms.يُعْتِقَ رَقَبَةً: to free a slave as expiation

ai.seo_question: What expiation is mentioned for someone who intentionally kills his slave?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal-ethical response to the intentional killing of one’s slave, mentioning expiatory acts of freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months, and feeding sixty needy people. It concludes by stressing tawbah, showing that legal expiation is joined with repentance before Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5261 - Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi that Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said

regarding a man who intentionally kills his slave:
"I prefer that he frees a slave, fasts for two consecutive months, and feeds sixty needy people, and then he should repent after that."
